To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

multilingual NMT models trained on multiple related languages can translate to unseen languages with reasonable quality and that the quality is higher when the unseen language is closer to the languages in the training set.

(1) a multilingual neural MT model can transfer weakly its knowledge to unseen languages, (2) the degree of knowledge transferability depends on languages' relatedness and (3) the limiting aspect of the multilingual architecture that causes weak transferability is that each language model is trained separately, without sharing parameters with other languages.
the transfer of the multilingual machine translation models is weak but possible and that it can be improved by using the multilingual word embeddings as a bridge between the languages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions. Can we transfer knowledge from a multilingual machine translation model to a language that is not part of the multilingual model?
two questions: (1) Can a multilingual neural MT model transfer to unseen languages?
the following questions: (1) Can a multilingual neural MT model be trained on a set of languages and then used to translate to a new language?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
multilingual NMT is a promising approach for cross lingual NLP.
cross lingual word representations are not sufficient to transfer the knowledge of a machine translation system to other languages.
the transfer is not zero shot, it is not even one shot but rather a few shot transfer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cross lingual word embedding can be used as a weak prior for multilingual translation.
we can achieve better zero shot translation performance by combining a monolingual translation model and a cross lingual embedding model.
cross lingual word embedding is a promising tool to improve multilingual machine translation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multilingual models can transfer knowledge to other languages even when they are not trained on them, but that the transferability depends heavily on the similarity of the languages.
the cross-lingual word embeddings can be used as a weak signal in the multilingual architectures for translation transfer.
multilingual models can be useful for low resource translation scenarios.
